correctness.rationale: The explicit degree-eight curve Q*xyz(y-z)(x-z)(x-r*y), r=9+4sqrt(5), has 3 nodes, 3 simple conic tangencies and 6 ordinary triple points, giving tau=36. At a new permissible seventh line, Bezout intersection degree 8 and local Tjurina gains prove delta tau=8+h+epsilon, where h is the number of old nodes met and epsilon flags one new simple conic tangency. Its three old nodes are noncollinear, so h<=2; exact conic restrictions to the three node-joining lines have nonzero discriminants (128, 3008+1344sqrt(5), 448+192sqrt(5)), so h=2 excludes epsilon=1. All 3 joins and exactly 3 noncomponent node-conic tangent lines avoid forbidden singularities, attain tau=46, and exhaust equality. For allowed singularity types, the published mdr>=4 and free/nearly-free degree-nine Tjurina values 48/47 exclude those extensions. The frozen source script was inspected; independent SymPy recomputed the conic determinant (-32), joins and dual tangent pencils. The symbolic certificate verifies the finite algebra, not the general geometric proof or literature.
